title: Japanese temple courtyard, golden hour (built with the Astra add-on)
_how_to_read: FINISHED for the reuse proof (21 October, 'Reuse - the same kit on the Japanese courtyard'): the designer's draft, with the changes the first pictures asked for (each one is written next to the key it changed as a _why note). Same keys as pit_village_street.json; nothing in the kit code repeats any of it. The courtyard has no plate camera yet, no 22-picture lighting test and no earlier layers, so those blocks stay as the draft left them.

growth.existing._note: 32,365 moss faces and 5,654 pebble faces the add-on already grew; used as a density picture, never doubled

stone.natural._note: 42 separate add-on materials (one per stone), each a 'FOUNDRY / Wet Stone' group with NO Principled box on the surface: needs the adapter. 61 to 72 faces each

stone.dressed._note: plain noise material; the plinth is a 10.9 x 5.6 m slab, top at z 0.55

timber.deck._note: 8 plank runs: .000-.002 veranda (planks run along y), .003-.007 bridge (planks run across). One plain Principled material per tone, no grain in the material

roof.tile._note: geometry nodes: the roof object has 42 faces; the tiles are 688 INSTANCES of one hidden 12-face tile. Layers read the surface in the shader or work on a realised copy

wall.plaster._note: 6-face boxes; the garden walls are 0.3 m thick, 2.1 to 2.2 m tall; every wall is an axis-aligned box in world space

wall.cap._note: 0.5 m wide dark tiled cap, 0.1 m overhang each side of the 0.3 m wall: the run-off source for the wall faces

bamboo._note: left alone in round one (0.5 % of the picture)

never._why: round 1 tried taking '^CT / ' off this list so the hidden roof-tile prototype could carry the roof's material: it made no difference (that object is not in the scene's object list at all), so the designer's list is back unchanged. See _findings_reuse_proof, item 1.

soot._note: in this set the layer is the dust-and-algae film, not soot (look file: film_mult near 1, tint grey-green)

wallgrowth._why: round 1: stone.natural added (moss, algae and lichen on the lantern, rocks and stepping stones).

dirt._why: round 1: stone.natural added (water marks and film on the stones).

ground._why: round 1: the plinth (stone.dressed, top at z 0.55) counts as ground, so the height of a post foot or a wall foot is measured from the plinth top. Without it every post foot is 0.55 m 'above the ground' and the foot layer (splash band, damp tide mark, rot) never reaches it. The tiny lantern finial is also stone.dressed and is skipped.

frames._front_note: explicit fronts (world directions): the garden back walls and the hall face the courtyard (-y), the right wall faces -x. Needed because earth runs under every wall, so the 'nearest ground' hint is undecided.

ground._note: The 'ground' section of the courtyard set file (see pit_village_street.json). The courtyard has no road, flags, kerbs or iron, so only the dirt and moss layers go on (gravel, earth, natural stone); every element the courtyard look leaves at 0 stays off. patch_moss is ON here (no joints to follow) and joint_share is OFF where there are no joints.

growth._note: The courtyard's growth section (first draft, to confirm in the courtyard job): moss cushions on earth, stones and the edge of the gravel, a little grass at the gravel edge; the add-on already grew moss and pebbles, so cushions leave most of the existing growth alone (existing_avoid) and the weeds dial of the kept look is 0.1.

_findings_reuse_proof: 1. ROOF: nothing can be painted onto the hall roof by settings. The roof is a geometry-nodes object with no material slot; its deck and ridge materials are set inside the modifier and its tile material sits on a hidden prototype object that is not in the scene's object list. The role finder (apply/roles.py describe_scene) only reads the material slots of objects in the scene, so no role can claim 'CT / Ceramic painterly surface', 'CT / Timber painterly surface' or 'CT / Ceramic ridge host-local surface'. Only the 3D growth pieces reach the roof (apply.growth.targets includes roof.tile, which realises the instances). Kit fix wanted: also read the evaluated object's materials and the instanced objects' materials.

2. WALL SHEETS: the long visible garden wall ('Right wall behind hall') gets no wall sheet: 'no wall face points toward the ground plan'. The front is chosen by the nearest ground point seen from the wall's middle (masks/wall_sheets.py _front_of); here the earth runs under every wall, so that point is straight below and the direction test is undecided. The designer's original pack failed the same way. Result: no run-off streak columns on that wall (the runoff layer changes under 0.5 percent of the picture). The Hall plaster sheet picked an end face (x axis), not the south face, and flipped sign when the plinth became ground. Kit fix wanted: an explicit front per frames entry in the settings.

3. ROLE DIALS: apply.<layer>.role_dials is read only by the soot layer (film_mult, sheltered_mult) among the walls layers. Entries written for foot and wallgrowth validate but do nothing, so lichen, moss or foot strength cannot differ between plaster, stone and wood. The look's one value per layer is used everywhere.

4. LICHEN: habitat.lichen.rough_stone_only is read by nothing (masks/habitat.py reads enabled and north_bias only), so lichen is not limited to rough stone; on pale plaster it shows as a speckle, so the look keeps lichen_amount low (0.2).

5. MOSS COLOUR: the wallgrowth moss is always at least 1.6 times as bright as the stone under it (a rule made for dark street stone). On mid-grey courtyard stone it comes out pale lime; the look keeps moss_amount at 0.6 and patch_moss low so grey stays visible. A moss darker than its stone is not possible by dials.

6. PLINTH AS GROUND: geometry.ground.roles now includes stone.dressed so heights (post feet, wall foot) are measured from the plinth top; the height picture shows the post feet at 0. No stain is visible at the post feet in the close view (dark timber, mostly in shade).
7. A plain settings_module.validate_look() on the look reports the builders' finer dials as unknown until apply() has registered the builders; apply() itself reports no problem.
